text: Dear Editor, I am writing to object to the council's decision to allow jet ski hire in Bluster Bay. For decades, the northern end of the bay has been a nesting beach for green turtles, and every summer, volunteers count the nests and fence them off. Since the hire shop opened in October, rangers have counted fourteen injured turtles, most with cuts on their shells that match the shape of a propeller. The hire shop is owned by a company called Gold Rush Rentals, which also sponsors Maxx Vantablack's channel. Each nest holds around a hundred eggs, and only a tiny number of hatchlings ever survive to become adults. When I raised this at the last council meeting, I was told the hire shop brings 'valuable tourism' to the town. A bay with fourteen injured turtles is no place for jet skis. The council's October decision was reckless and short-sighted, and it was made without asking a single local. Surely nobody wants to see a turtle hurt for the sake of a joyride. Bluster Bay is far too precious to be ruined by noisy machines. I urge every reader to come to the council meeting on 12 December and make their voice heard. Yours faithfully, Ada Pennick, turtle volunteer

text: SCIENCE FAIR REPORT: Which food grows mould fastest? by Gus. I left five foods in sealed jars on the windowsill of the Soggy Biscuit's galley for fourteen days: white bread, an orange, cheese, a boiled potato and one of Mo's fish-finger custards. I photographed each jar at the same time every morning and measured how much of the surface was covered in mould. Before starting, I predicted that the cheese would grow mould first, because it already smells like feet. The bread was the first to grow mould, with fluffy green spots appearing on day three. By day ten, the orange was completely covered in a blue-green fuzz. The cheese grew the least mould of the real foods. Mo's custard grew no mould at all, which I find deeply worrying. The potato grew a small patch of white mould on day seven, which Wren said looked like a tiny snowfield. Next time, I would like to test whether mould grows faster in the dark. In my opinion, mould is the most fascinating life form on the planet, and every school should have a mould garden. The smell in the galley on day fourteen was so strong that Tully moved her hammock onto the deck.
